In addition, a FS-TCC with 45-53µm conductive microsphere inclusions (thickness: 140 ± 20µm) upholds a permeability of 0.80 ± 0.122 g·mm/m2/day (WVTR of 5.74 ± 0.287 g/m2/day) when measured as-synthesized and without aging. A separate sample set was prepared and evaluated for permeabilities after 1,000 hours of damp heat exposure (85°C in 85% R.H. in dark). A laminate sample (thickness: 315 µm ± 55µm) served as the benchmark, which demonstrated a slightly lower permeability of 0.48 ± 0.088 g·mm/m2/day (WVTR of 1.53 ± 0.077 g/m2/day) as compared to the as- synthesized sample. In conjunction, FS-TCC samples with 500-520µm Ag-PMMA inclusions (thickness: 530 ± 55µm) and 45-53µm Ag-PMMA inclusions (thickness: 110 ± 30µm) subjected to 1,000 hours of damp heat exposure measured comparable permeabilities of 0.58 ± 0.067 g·mm/m2/day (WVTR of 1.10 ± 0.055 g/m2/day) and 0.52 ± 0.143 g·mm/m2/day (WVTR of 4.69 ± 0.235 g/m2/day), respectively. Although the calculated permeabilities include slight errors due to variations in thickness, they serve as a useful metric to evaluate performance across samples of different thicknesses and compositions. Notably, as-synthesized laminates and FS-TCCs measure permeabilities of approximately 0.8 g·mm/m2/day regardless of microsphere inclusions and size, indicating that the effects from the addition of microsphere inclusions do not dominate the permeation. Furthermore, permeabilities across aged laminates and FS-TCCs (approx. 0.5 g·mm/m2/day) indicate resilience under damp heat and confirm the integrity of the microsphere-epoxy interface after 1,000 hours of accelerated aging.
